clue.text: Call time in race after gold decorative work

indicators.note: the call-time-in-race part comes after gold, so gold leads

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold
to call someone something is to name them

indicators.note: in tells us the time letter goes inside the word for race

parts.note: a race of people is a nation

explanation.surface: A command to summon time in a race, following a gold medal, dressed up as craftwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornamentation is embellishment added to an object, which is exactly decorative work.

clue.text: Protector has girl generously taken round Catholic city endlessly

indicators.note: the girl and generously pieces are wrapped around the Catholic city part

parts.note: Olive is a girl's name
to give well is to give generously
RC is the abbreviation for Roman Catholic

indicators.note: endlessly drops the final letter of the city's name

parts.note: Rome is the Catholic city

explanation.surface: A guardian whose girlfriend has been lavishly escorted around a Catholic city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken round' wraps the girl and generously pieces around the Catholic city part; 'endlessly' trims the final E of Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Cromwell ruled England as Lord Protector in the 1650s, so the title alone identifies him.

clue.text: And not the old point

parts.note: nor means and not, as in neither this nor that
th' is the old poetic contraction of the, as in th'expense

explanation.surface: A puzzled denial that something is the old point being made.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the four cardinal points of the compass.

clue.text: Check or age vehicle

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness check on British vehicles
taken as written
a cycle can mean a long age or era

explanation.surface: Instructions to check a vehicle's condition or its age.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's yearly compulsory test of a vehicle's safety.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorbike is a two-wheeled powered vehicle, so vehicle is its general class.

clue.text: Clear increase of wild gentian

indicators.note: wild says the letters of gentian run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A clear rise in the number of wild gentian flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A net gain is a profit left after deductions, an unambiguous increase.

clue.text: Tune is following the latest trends in this vehicle

parts.note: a tune is an air, so tune is becomes air's
someone hip keeps up with the latest fashions

explanation.surface: A fashionable tune is playing in some vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirigible is a powered lighter-than-air craft, a flying vehicle.

clue.text: Small measure for Scottish island

definitions.meaning: a unit of length a twelfth of a foot
in Scotland the word is used for a small island, as in Inchcolm

explanation.surface: A tiny unit of length suited to a small Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an imperial length unit and a Scots term for an islet.

clue.text: Old type size like no other

definitions.meaning: a former printers' size of type, about six point

explanation.surface: An outdated printing size described as unique.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a historic six-point type and also means matchless or without equal.

clue.text: Tailor-made tent prepared for ragamuffin

indicators.note: prepared says these letters are made ready in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A custom tent got ready to house a scruffy urchin.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a person in ragged, tattered clothes.

clue.text: One who annoys water provider using tons, not gallons

indicators.note: using the tons letter in place of another one
not marks the gallons letter as the one dropped

parts.note: an irrigator supplies water to land

explanation.surface: An annoying person who waters with tons rather than gallons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Using' tons, 'not' gallons: swap the G of IRRIGATOR for a T.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who irritates others is an annoyer, one who provokes.

clue.text: Plant that grows in tropics isn't able to in Scotland

definitions.meaning: a tropical flowering plant with large leaves, also called Indian shot

explanation.surface: A tropical plant that cannot survive in the Scottish climate.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a tropical lily-like plant genus and is also Scots dialect for cannot.

clue.text: The setter must leave one or other in the upper air

indicators.note: must leave means the setter's letter departs the other word

parts.note: either means one or the other
the setter refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: The compiler has to leave one way or another, flying off into the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: In old cosmology the ether was the clear upper sky above the clouds.

clue.text: Do not start to hide pain

indicators.note: do not start says the first letter of the hide word is dropped

parts.note: to cache something is to hide it

explanation.surface: Advice not to begin concealing your pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull continuing pain is a synonym of the word.

clue.text: Pointe?

parts.note: read as point E: the compass point that the letter E stands for, disguised as the ballet word for dancing on the toes

explanation.walkthrough: Pointe, the ballet position, splits into point plus E, which is the abbreviation for this compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: E is the standard abbreviation for this compass direction, so it is the point E.

clue.text: Pope found in her hayloft perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: The pontiff discovered hiding in a woman's hayloft.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pope is addressed by Catholics with this title of reverence.

clue.text: Continue in some films

definitions.meaning: the ... films, a long-running series of bawdy British comedies

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep going in certain movies.
explanation.walkthrough: The Carry On films are a series of over thirty British comedy films made from 1958 onwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means keep going and is also the title prefix of a British comedy film series.

clue.text: Old publicity displayed during journeys to find places along the way?

indicators.note: displayed during puts the old publicity in the middle of the journeys

parts.note: rides are journeys
ads are advertisements, publicity

explanation.surface: Old advertisements shown on trips, seen at spots beside the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Verges and spots beside a road are places lying along the route, with the question mark for the punning way.

clue.text: Trailblazer having one in support

indicators.note: in puts the one inside the support word

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar of a bridge

explanation.surface: A trailblazer with somebody backing them.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is the first to explore new ground, a trailblazer by definition.

clue.text: Men left among experts; they speak divinely

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: among places the left letter inside the experts

parts.note: aces are experts

explanation.surface: Men abandoned among specialists, who talk in a heavenly way.
explanation.definitionFit: Oracles in ancient Greece were channels through which the gods spoke.

clue.text: Make a quick profit with the Spanish knife

parts.note: to scalp is to resell for a fast profit
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Turning a quick buck on a Spanish blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon's small sharp blade is a kind of knife.

clue.text: Imaginary colour (not pink) of oar at Cambridge?

definitions.meaning: as in blue-sky thinking, unconstrained and fanciful

definitions.text: colour (not pink) of oar at Cambridge?
definitions.meaning: Cambridge's rowing colour is light blue; not pink, as pink is a different kind of oarsman's colour at Leander

explanation.surface: A fanciful hue for a Cambridge rowing oar, rather than pink.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge University's sporting colour is a pale blue, as opposed to Oxford's dark blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale azure is the hue of Cambridge oars, and the word also means fanciful, as in visionary ideas.

clue.text: Social level of Italian restaurant in substance

indicators.note: in places the restaurant inside the substance word

parts.note: sum as in the gist or substance of something
trat is short for trattoria

explanation.surface: The class of person found at an Italian restaurant, in essence.
explanation.definitionFit: A social stratum is a layer or class within society.

clue.text: What initially in Paris is the point?

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: est is French for is

explanation.surface: A query about what, in Paris, the point is.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the four cardinal compass directions.

clue.text: Den that's regularly leafier

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A den that is consistently more leafy.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild animal's den is its lair, its hiding place.

clue.text: Tea as organised? Far from it

indicators.note: organised calls for the letters to be put into a new order

explanation.surface: Was the tea arranged? Not remotely.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads off the question: being bewildered is the very opposite of organised.
explanation.definitionFit: To be confused and lost is to be far from organised, an idiom from being out of sight of land.

clue.text: So do Hotpoint?

parts.note: taken as written
ut is the old name for the note do in sol-fa
the brand name splits into hot and point: H stands for hot, as on taps, and point is the definition

explanation.surface: A question about a Hotpoint appliance.
explanation.walkthrough: Hotpoint is a British brand of household appliances; split as Hot and point it gives H and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the four cardinal compass directions.

clue.text: Two notes? Simple!

definitions.meaning: me and re are two notes of the sol-fa scale, written together
nothing more than, as in a simple slip

explanation.definitionFit: Mere means nothing more than, simple, as in a simple oversight.

clue.text: Spoon the French boy? The reverse

indicators.note: the reverse says the two pieces go in the opposite order to the clue

parts.note: a lad is a boy
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Is the spoon the French boy? Rather the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep long-handled serving spoon for soup.

clue.text: Aromatic shrub in beauty spot essentially ghoulish

parts.note: a patch is a small black spot worn on the face as a beauty mark

indicators.note: essentially takes the central letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A fragrant bush in a lovely place, fundamentally creepy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beauty spot' tempts as a pretty location; it is the face patch.
explanation.definitionFit: Patchouli is an Asian plant of the mint family grown for its fragrant oil.

clue.text: Gain an advantage over some charlatan criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are corrupted into a new order

explanation.surface: Getting the better of a crooked swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from military use, moving troops ahead secretly to get ahead of an enemy.
